9927.t: From ὑποκρίνομαι (hŭpokrī́nomai, “to answer (a fellow actor on stage), play a part, feign, pretend”) + -σις (-sĭs).

9940.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *wed- Proto-Indo-European *-rós Proto-Indo-European *udrós Proto-Indo-European *udréh₂ Proto-Hellenic *údrā Ancient Greek ὕδρα From Proto-Hellenic *údrā, from Proto-Indo-European *udréh₂, the feminine form of *udrós, from…

9926.t: From ὑποτίθημι (hŭpotĭ́thēmĭ, “to place under, set before, suggest”) + -σις (-sĭs).

9954.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *ehonts, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁sónts, present participle of *h₁es- (“to be”).

9968.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ser-? Proto-Indo-European *srew- Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ Proto-Indo-European *sréwmn̥? Proto-Hellenic *hréumə Ancient Greek ῥεῦμα From Proto-Hellenic *hréumə, likely inherited from Proto-Indo-European *sréwmn̥, from…

9939.t: According to Furnée, a Pre-Greek word, due to the variation "α/ε".

9975.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hrówos, from Proto-Indo-European *srówos, from *srew- (“to flow”). Cognate with Sanskrit स्रव (srava), Latvian strava, Lithuanian sravà, Proto-Slavic *ostrovъ.

9979.t: Traditionally derived from ῥέπω (rhépō, “to decline, descend”), but perhaps not related to the verb.

9981.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sríHgos and cognate with Latin frīgus (“cold, frost”).

9941.t: From Proto-Indo-European *súpr̥, generalized from the zero-grade of an r/n-stem of *swep- (“to sleep”) + *-r̥, whence also ὕπνος (hŭ́pnos, “sleep”).

9958.t: From ϝρήν (wrḗn), the old nominative of ϝάρνα (wárna), ϝαρνός (warnós), etc., for which see ἀρήν (arḗn); compare πολύρρην (polúrrhēn), ῥᾶνα (rhâna), and τρανόν (tranón), the last perhaps from ϝρᾶνον (wrânon).

9955.t: From the same root as ὠχρός (ōkhrós, “pale yellow”).

9980.t: From the verb ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow; to stream”).

9978.t: From ῥαπίζω (rhapízō, “to strike, thrash, cudgel, hit, slap”) + -μα (-ma).

9928.t: From ὑπολαμβάνω (hupolambánō, “to take up, grasp, interpret”) + -σις (-sĭs).

9946.t: From Old Persian 𐎺𐎼𐎣𐎠𐎴 (v-r-k-a-n /⁠Vr̥kānaʰ⁠/), from 𐎺𐎼𐎣 (v-r-k /⁠vr̥kaʰ⁠⁠/, “wolf”), from Proto-Indo-European *wĺ̥kʷos, whence also λύκος (lúkos). Cognate with Avestan 𐬬𐬆𐬵𐬭𐬐𐬁𐬥𐬀 (vəhrkāna) and Parthian 𐭅𐭓𐭊𐭍 (wrkn /⁠Wurgān⁠/).
